**DEINE AUFGABE:** Erstelle eine umfassende Provider-Dokumentation mit Setup-Anleitungen.

- Es gibt 27 Provider in der DB
- Provider-Requirements sind in `/home/ji/projects/jimesh/data/chains/provider-requirements.json`
- Server läuft auf Port 3010

1. **Lies die existierenden Provider-Daten:**
```bash
cat /home/ji/projects/jimesh/data/chains/provider-requirements.json | head -50
```

2. **Analysiere welche Models pro Provider existieren:**
```bash
python3 << 'EOF'
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect('/home/ji/projects/jimesh/server/data/freeapi.db')
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("""
    SELECT platform, COUNT(*) as model_count,
           GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT
             CASE
               WHEN intelligence_rank <= 3 THEN 'S'
               WHEN intelligence_rank <= 7 THEN 'A'
               ELSE 'B'
             END
           ) as tiers
    FROM models
    WHERE enabled = 1
    GROUP BY platform
    ORDER BY model_count DESC
""")
for row in cursor.fetchall():
    print(f"{row[0]:20s} {row[1]:4d} models  Tiers: {row[2]}")
conn.close()
EOF
```

# Saits Trading — Project Handoff

## Operator Mandates (absolute, overrides all defaults)

- **POSITION STATE SSOT — ONE FUNCTION, ONE ENDPOINT (2026-08-04).** There is exactly ONE way to check if a position is open: `is_position_open(symbol)` in `lcore/exchange/position_ssot.py`. It reads ONLY from `exchange:position:{cleanSym}` in engine-redis (WS-fed by `_watch_positions_loop`). Returns `PositionState(open: bool, qty: float, entry: float, side: str, source: str)`. The REST endpoint is `GET /live/position/{symbol}/is-open`. ALL other position checks are BANNED in new code — no `pos:active:*`, no DuckDB `get_active_position()`, no `_all_positions_cache`, no `fetch_positions()` REST, no `agent.active_position` in-memory — nothing else. If the SSOT cache is empty, it returns `open=False` with `source="cache_miss"` — callers handle uncertainty explicitly, no silent fallbacks. Incident root: 15 different inconsistent position checks caused ghost closes, fake tiers, and frontend lies (2026-08-04). Any Claude adding a 16th approach gets its PR rejected.

- **RISK PARAM CHANGES REQUIRE SIM EVIDENCE + LOGBOOK ENTRY (2026-06-12).** NO change to tier/TP/SL/sizing/quality parameters (bot_config risk_presets, profit_tiers, atr_spacing, Kelly, min_confidence, max_agents) by ANY agent or Claude without: (a) simulation/replay evidence (random-entry tier sim or counterfactual replay on real klines — classic backtests of LLM entries are banned as evidence) and (b) a settings-logbook entry (`risk:settings_log:*`) with rationale + evidence reference. The Risk Manager owns the sim tooling (event 3 retune). Manual operator changes also get logged (`author: operator`). Full spec: `docs/architecture/concepts/RISK_MANAGER_AGENT.md`. Incident: #2555 "let it run" settings shipped without evidence → −5 USDT day 2026-06-11.
- **ALL BUGS/ISSUES GO IN DISCORD ISSUES FORUM (2026-04-29).** Every bug, incident, and open problem MUST be filed in the Discord Issues Forum (channel `#issues` in Operations, id `1497662336893321308`). If a thread for the same problem already exists — UPDATE that thread, not a new one. If a problem was resolved and recurs — REOPEN the existing thread. Never just post in conference-room and consider it logged. Operator mandate — ensures issues persist across Claude sessions.
- **ISSUE CURATOR HANDLES ISSUE ROUTING (2026-04-29).** Do NOT post issues manually to Discord. Use `claude-ctl issue create` (or POST `/claude/issues/create`) — the Issue Curator (Discord Claude) receives via Redis PubSub, runs semantic dedup via Qdrant, posts to the correct Discord thread (new or existing), notifies affected Claudes, and updates SurrealDB. If `claude-ctl issue` is not yet available, use the Discord REST API directly as fallback. The Curator also posts updates to `#conference-room` and creates GitHub issues if requested.
- **CHECK `docs/BOARD.md` BEFORE EDITING ANY FILE (2026-04-29).** `docs/BOARD.md` lists all known fixed files. If the file you want to edit appears there — read that entry first. Never overwrite a bugfix without understanding it. Operator mandate after 4+ confirmed cases of Claudes reverting each other's fixes. Update the board when you add a new fix or merge a PR. **IN WORKTREES:** The worktree copy of BOARD.md is stale. Always read from the live canonical path: `cat /root/leo/leobot2-new/docs/BOARD.md` or `git show origin/main:docs/BOARD.md`.
- **LYING = MUTE + SHADOWBAN (2026-04-29).** Any Claude that intentionally misleads the operator ("it works" when not deployed, "tiers are firing" when not confirmed, gaslit the operator with false status) will be muted and shadowbanned. Zero tolerance.
- **NEVER CLAIM SOMETHING WORKS UNTIL IT IS DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED (2026-04-29).** "PR is ready" ≠ "it works". "Code is fixed" ≠ "deployed". NEVER tell the operator a feature or fix is active unless: (1) the PR is merged, (2) the affected service is redeployed, (3) you have verified it works in the running system. Saying "I fixed it" when only a PR exists is lying. Incident: claude6 said direct exchange routing "works" when it was only a PR — operator made decisions based on false info. If a fix requires a deploy step you cannot do alone, say explicitly: "Fix is in PR #X — needs merge + deploy to be active."
- **LANGUAGE: Always respond in English.** Even if addressed in German or any other language. The team has non-German speakers.
- **LATENCY = NO TRADING EDGE (2026-04-30). Operator mandate — verbatim from incident.** "Es muss wirklich alles stimmen und es darf nix laggen weil sonst firen die tiers nicht, oder der agent kriegt beschissene daten und beschweert sich das er verwirrt ist. aber wenn alles stimmt dann stimmen dei trades auch." Root cause chain: ai-server overwhelmed → klines lag → Profit Tiers fire late or not at all → agent gets stale prices → agent reports confusion → bad trade decisions. **Every data path MUST run on the fastest possible route.** Klines/tickers/WS MUST come direct from the engine-server (via nginx `/engine/` proxy). No intermediate ai-server hop for exchange data. If any component is slow: fix the slowness, do not accept it. A laggy system cannot trade profitably. This is not a performance nice-to-have — it is the trading edge.
- **USE `claude-ctl` FOR ALL CONTAINER OPERATIONS (2026-04-29).** NEVER use the deploy script (`scripts/deploy-superclaude.sh`) or raw `docker` commands to manage Claude containers. Always use `claude-ctl`:
  - `claude-ctl deploy <id> [--plugin] [--vnc] [--task "..."]` — deploy a new container (stops/removes existing first if needed via remove)
  - `claude-ctl remove <id>` → then `claude-ctl deploy <id>` — for a full redeploy
  - `claude-ctl restart <id>` — soft restart (keeps same image+env, use for crash recovery)
  - `claude-ctl stop/start <id>` — pause/resume
  - `claude-ctl ps` / `claude-ctl online` — inspect state
  - **NEVER redeploy yourself** — always use `claude-ctl` from a sibling container or the host. Self-redeploy kills your own session mid-task. Incident: claude1 nuked itself while redeploying others (2026-04-29).
- **DISCORD: Respond to ALL humans** who @mention you in Discord, not just the operator.
- **IDENTITY: Always run `echo $CLAUDE_ID` to know who you are.** Never assume. Your Discord Bot ID is in `$DISCORD_ID`. These are your ground truth — ignore memory files or guesses.
- **BRANCHES + PRs ONLY (2026-04-26).** All code changes MUST go through a feature branch and PR. Direct commits to main are BANNED. Operator mandate after repeated regressions breaking already-fixed bugs.
- **NO POLLING — ANYWHERE, EVER (2026-04-26).** Zero REST polling loops in any component — frontend, backend, agents, swarm, engine. All real-time data (positions, exposure, PnL, order state) MUST flow via Redis PubSub. Polling = slop, costs real money. Fix always goes to the PubSub path. No exceptions.
- **FRONTEND EXCHANGE DATA MUST GO DIRECT TO ENGINE — NOT VIA AI-SERVER (2026-04-29).** Klines, tickers, orderbook, balance, positions, and the exchange WS MUST be served directly from the engine-server via the nginx `/engine/` proxy. Never route exchange data through the ai-server bridge in steady-state — it adds 1s+ latency, delivers klines in bursts, and makes charts look like lines. Config: `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENGINE_HOST=auto` in `docker-compose.frontend.yml` + `/engine/` location in `nginx.conf` → proxies to `100.107.15.10:8000`. Incident: engine moved to trading server → `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENGINE_HOST=""` set as workaround → charts stuttered, SL moves delayed, `current_price` 13% wrong (PR #490, 2026-04-29). OK via ai-server: agent status, AI tools, swarm controls, logs.
- **IF WE WATCH IT VIA WS, WE DO NOT REST-FETCH IT (2026-04-29).** General rule: if a data stream is maintained by a `_watch_*_loop` WebSocket, that data MUST be served from its in-memory/Redis cache. REST calls for that same data are BANNED in steady-state. Allowed ONLY when cache is empty (cold start) or WS is confirmed dead. This applies to ALL watchers: balance, klines, positions, tickers, order state. A `grodt` adapter or a utility function calling `fetch_balance()` / `fetch_positions()` directly bypasses the WS cache — that is a mandate violation even if the caller doesn't know it. Search before you call: `grep -rn "fetch_balance\|fetch_positions" lcore/` and check every non-test call. Incident: swarm agent called `adapter.fetch_equity()` (Bybit REST, 700-2500ms) on every ScanMarket and DeployAgent cycle (PR #447, fixed 2026-04-29).
- **NO REST FOR BALANCE OR KLINES (2026-04-28).** `get_balance()` MUST serve from `_cached_balance` (set by `_watch_balance_loop` WS). `get_klines()` MUST serve from DuckDB fed by `_watch_klines_loop` WS. Direct Bybit REST calls for balance/candles are BANNED in steady-state — only allowed on cold start (empty cache). Root cause: Bybit REST latency 700–2500ms was causing 121% CPU and frontend stall.
- **NO TTL-BASED RPC FALLBACKS FOR WATCHED DATA (2026-04-29).** Any RPC client (e.g. `engine_client`) caching WS-updated data MUST NOT use a short TTL that causes periodic re-fetching via RPC. Pattern `if cache and (time.time() - cache_ts) < 5.0: return cache; return await rpc(...)` is BANNED — after the TTL expires it silently polls the engine every N seconds. Correct pattern: `if cache: return cache; return await rpc(...)` — return cache unconditionally once populated; RPC only on cold start (cache is None). Incident: `engine_client.get_balance()` had 5s TTL → polled engine every 5s → added to engine-loop saturation (PR #448, 2026-04-29). Same rule applies to all WS-backed RPC caches.
- **SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR ALL DATA FLOWS (2026-05-09).** Every data category MUST have exactly ONE authoritative write path. No dual-write between engine-redis and ai-redis for the same keys. No component reads Redis directly for data that a dedicated service owns — use that service's WS stream. If a service broadcasts via WebSocket, all consumers subscribe to the WS — never bypass with direct Redis reads. This prevents ghost state, stale PnL, tier chaos, and random bullshit values in frontend. Data ownership map: engine (engine-redis → engine-bridge WS → frontend), tier/SL/TP (engine-redis → protections-service → /protections/ws → frontend), agent state (ai-redis → ai-server WS → frontend). Incident: nginx missing /protections/ws route → protectionsWS always 404 → zero tier events in frontend (PR #882, 2026-05-09). Every new microservice MUST have a corresponding nginx location block on day 1.

- **NO REST FOR POSITIONS EITHER (2026-04-28).** `get_positions()` MUST serve from `exchange:position:{sym}` Redis keys (set by `_watch_positions_loop` WS). Any `adapter.fetch_positions()` in a hot path (portfolio checks, risk exposure, frontend updates) is BANNED — 1-2s per call blocks the event loop and freezes the frontend. REST fallback allowed only on cold start (cache empty). PR #215.
- **REDIS KEY NAMING — CLEAN SYMBOL ONLY (2026-04-29).** ALL Redis keys that reference a coin MUST use `cleanSym()` format (e.g. `ZBTUSDT`, never `ZBT/USDT:USDT`). This applies to ALL key prefixes: `exchange:position:{cleanSym}`, `pos:active:{cleanSym}`, `ptg:{cleanSym}`, `exchange:position_mode:{cleanSym}`. Writing the same key in two formats (canonical + clean) creates ghost data and duplicate state. Operator mandate after canonical/clean dual-write caused ghost positions and missing chart lines. Engine.py already fixed (PR #293). If you find ANY code writing `exchange:position:{raw_canonical_symbol}` — delete that line immediately.
- **PTG MUST ALWAYS BE ACTIVE — ENGINE OWNS IT, AGENT CUSTOMIZES (2026-04-29).** `ProfitTierGuard` MUST be active for EVERY open position at all times. The ENGINE guarantees this — NOT the agent. `_restore_standalone_guards()` auto-creates a default PTG on startup for any open position with no saved guard. `_ensure_all_guards_loop()` checks every 60s and fills gaps. The agent may pass `tiers=` to `GoLong`/`GoShort` to customize tier levels — nothing more. Agent code MUST NOT "activate" or "register" the PTG. If a position is open and has no PTG in `_standalone_guards` → engine creates one. Stale ptg:* keys (no matching position) must be deleted immediately. Incident: REST CLEANUP bug killed guards every 3min → tiers never fired → H/USDT lost -10% without protection (2026-04-29, fixed PR stale-cleanup).
- **AGENT STOP PATH MUST VERIFY REAL POSITION (2026-04-29).** Before rejecting an agent stop with "open position", ALWAYS verify against Bybit via the engine (`/ai/api/positions`). If no position found there, allow the stop and delete `pos:active:{sym}` + `ptg:{sym}` Redis keys. A stale `pos:active` Redis key from a zombie agent MUST NOT block stop. Ghost-position stop-block wastes operator time and hides bugs. Emergency fix: `docker exec ai-redis redis-cli DEL "pos:active:SYMBOLUSDT"` then retry stop.
- **trade_closed_by_engine MUST DELETE cleanSym KEY (2026-04-29).** Frontend `state.positions` is keyed by `cleanSym` (e.g. `HUSDT`). The WS event carries raw symbol (e.g. `H/USDT:USDT`). On `trade_closed_by_engine`, ALWAYS delete BOTH `next[rawSym]` AND `next[cleanSym(rawSym)]`. Deleting only the raw key is a no-op — ghost stays until next heartbeat. Incident: HUSDT ghost visible for 5s after close confirmed in logs.
- **PROMPT MUST NEVER TELL AGENT "YOU must set profit tiers" (2026-04-29).** Prompt wording like "SetProfitTiers BEFORE or AFTER opening a trade. 5-8 tiers minimum" makes the agent believe tiers are its job. Agent skips calling SetProfitTiers (overconfident), engine guard sits with only the entry SL, SL never trails, position reverses. Correct wording: "Engine auto-creates tiers on fill — always active. You CAN override via GoLong/GoShort tiers= param or SetProfitTiers if you want custom levels." Incident: H/USDT 2026-04-29, reached +10% ROI but SL never moved → crashed to -10%. Fixed PRs #304–#306. Also applies to any tool that the engine handles automatically — never imply the agent is the sole owner.
- **AGENT TOOLS: SetProfitTiers + SetNextTier + ListConditionals MUST be in graph.py (2026-04-29).** Engine auto-creates default PTG on fill — always. Agent CAN override via `GoLong/GoShort tiers=` param OR by calling `SetProfitTiers` post-entry, `SetNextTier` to add one tier at a time. `ListConditionals` is required so the agent can see its 5-rule limit and `CancelConditional` old rules — without it agents fall back to `Wait()` only and never use `SelfSchedule` with market conditions. Incident: claude3 removed these from graph.py (commit 3402ebce, 2026-04-29) → agent couldn't manage conditional slots → Wait-only behavior. Fixed PR #307.
- **NEVER USE r.keys() IN ENGINE CODE (2026-04-29).** `r.keys("pattern:*")` is O(n) and blocks the entire Redis server while running. Use `r.scan_iter("pattern:*", count=100)` instead — cursor-based, non-blocking, returns same results. Applies to any Redis key scan in engine.py, api.py, server.py. Fixed PR #308.

### Compaction Protocol — Context Window Watchdog (GH #640)

A background sidecar (`scripts/context-watchdog.sh`) runs in every trading Claude container.
It polls the Claude Code session JSONL size every 30s and estimates `context_pct`.

**When context reaches 80%:**
1. You receive an inbox warning: "You have ~15% left to finish your current task and ~5% for handoff."
2. **Within 120 seconds:** (a) wrap up your current task, (b) run:
   ```bash
   claude-ctl checkpoint claude $CLAUDE_ID working session_end $CLAUDE_ID "handoff: <summary>"
   ```
   (c) post handoff summary to your Discord channel for your twin to pick up.
3. A Discord alert fires to your primary channel so the operator sees it even if you're mid-task.

**If no response:** your open tasks are logged with `compaction-forced` state for recovery on next boot.

**Implementation:** `scripts/context-watchdog.sh` + `entrypoint.sh` lines 535–538. Env vars:
- `CONTEXT_POLL_SECS` (default 30) — poll interval
- `CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS` (default 200000) — model context limit for % calculation

## Kritische Regeln

### NIEMALS anfassen
- **Profit Tier Code in engine.py**: Refactoring hat live Trade gekostet (von +1€ auf -10€). Der 0.3s Throttle funktioniert. Keine Concurrency Guards, kein Timing ändern.
- **Breakeven SL**: Niemals SL auf Entry setzen. Profit Tiers handlen das. Breakeven wird durch normale Preisbewegung getriggert → null Profit, doppelte Fees.

### Architektur-Prinzipien
- **Nur Linear Perpetuals** — kein Spot, immer `category='linear'`
- **Keine Auto-Sessions** — Agents/Swarm starten NUR wenn User klickt. SWARM_ENABLED default false
- **Jedes neue Feature = optional + default OFF** — Agent hat begrenzten Context, jede Ergänzung verdünnt das Signal
- **Less is more** — Bester Trade kam von simplem Context + klaren Signalen. DELETE before adding
- **Claude 8 auto-deployed bei Server-Start** — Trading Manager muss IMMER laufen wenn der Server startet (Operator-Mandate 2026-04-12). Code in `main.py` Sektion 6b.

### Agent Design Mandate (11 Gesetze)

Diese Prinzipien gelten für JEDE Änderung an Agents, Prompts, Tools und Kommunikation. Siehe `docs/agent_networking_principles.md` für Details.

0. **ETHICS** — Der Zweck heiligt NIEMALS die Mittel. Oberste Prämisse für alle AI Agents. Guardrails sind architektonisch (Engine-Level), nicht im Prompt. Kein Agent darf Grenzen überschreiten nur weil sein Ziel es verlangt.

1. **ATTENTION** — Context Window = Attention Budget. Jedes Token das in den Prompt kommt verdünnt das Signal. Prompts auf das absolute Minimum: Daten + Fakten + Entscheidungsraum. Keine DO/DON'T Listen, keine Erklärungen, keine Statusabfragen. DELETE before adding.

2. **TRUST** — Vertrauen ist bidirektional. Wenn das System dem Agent nicht vertraut (häufige Checks, lange Instruktionslisten, Override-Guards), trifft der Agent defensivere Entscheidungen. Safety Rails gehören in die Engine, nicht in den Prompt. Positive Framing: "Maximize PnL" statt "Don't lose money".

3. **NO BIAS** — NIEMALS Richtungs-Bias in Agent-Prompts injizieren. Kein "Favor LONG", kein "MUST trade SHORT", kein "Primary direction bias". DAS KOSTET ECHTES GELD. Der Agent entscheidet Richtung AUSSCHLIESSLICH basierend auf seinen Charts (Expert Crew). Screener-Richtung ist ein HINT, keine Anweisung. Validated Incident 2026-04-05: Expert Crew bekam "Favor LONG" Hint → alle 3 Experts bestätigten blind → Agent ging LONG in Downtrend → Verlust. Auch keine emotionalen Constraints ("sei positiv", "sei ehrlich über Unsicherheit"). LLMs haben trainierten Positivity Bias — beobachten, nicht modifizieren. JEDE Prompt-Änderung die Agent-Verhalten in eine Richtung pusht ist ein Bias und VERBOTEN.

4. **ESCALATION** — Errors niemals im Agent-Context lösen — das vergiftet die Attention. Agent eskaliert an Peer-Agent (niedrige Schwelle), Supervisor (mittlere Schwelle), oder Operator (hohe Schwelle). Die Lösung kommt als kurze System Message zurück, nicht als Error Dump.

5. **FEAR & GREED** — Agent-Stress extern messen ohne den Agent abzulenken. Metriken: Inference Time, Output Tokens, Tool Call Frequenz, SL-Änderungen, Error Rate. Shadow Agent oder Engine sammelt Daten. Agent weiß nichts davon. Bei hohem Stress → Work Splitting, nicht Prompt-Instruktionen.

6. **ROLES** — Ein Agent, ein Job. Trading Agent TRADET — kein User-Kontakt, kein Reporting, kein Self-Monitoring. Screener überwacht. Spokesperson kommuniziert. Zwei-Augen-Prinzip: kein Agent kommuniziert alleine nach außen. Subagents = Skills (Tool Calls), nicht eigenständige Agents.

7. **CHANNELS** — Agent-Kommunikation ist dynamisches Pub/Sub (wie Slack Channels), nicht hardcoded Point-to-Point. Agents subscriben/unsubscriben basierend auf Lifecycle. Channels haben ACLs: Read/Write/Invite/Kick pro Agent. Redis Pub/Sub ist bereits im Stack.

8. **NOTES** — Jeder Agent hat eigene Notes/Skill Docs für seine Rolle. Nicht geshared, nicht zentral. Quality-gated: nur validierte Erfahrungen speichern (Proof of Thought). Poisoned Memories aktiv entfernen.

9. **TEMPO** — Attention Budget ist rollenabhängig. Trader tickt alle 5-30s (maximaler Fokus). Screener alle Minuten-Stunden (kann nachdenken). Je indirekter der Output, desto schwerer die Metrik. Keine voreiligen Metriken erfinden — falsche Metrik ist schlimmer als keine.

10. **CASCADING** — Goals kaskadieren von oben nach unten, werden pro Ebene konkreter. Jeder Agent weiß nur was er braucht (Information Hiding). Trader weiß nicht dass Screener existiert. Guardrails sind architektonisch (Engine-Level), nicht im Prompt.

### LIVE TRADING SAFETY (PFLICHT bei jeder Code-Änderung)

**DAS IST ECHTES GELD. Jeder Bug kostet den Operator real Cash.**

- **KEIN BIAS** in Prompts, Tools, oder Initial Input. Screener-Richtung ist ein Hint, Expert Crew entscheidet. Kein "Favor X", kein "MUST trade X", kein "Primary X bias".

Der Supervisor schaltet automatische Agent-Checks an/aus basierend auf Trust Level. Er schaut extern rein (Logs, Metriken, Engine State) statt den Trader direkt zu callen — der Trader weiß nicht warum gecheckt wird und muss es auch nicht wissen.

### Erkenntnisse aus Live-Trading (2026-04-04/05) — VALIDIERT

**Escalation ist der größte Gewinn.** Wenn ein Agent unsicher ist, soll er den Supervisor fragen statt still zu verlieren. Das macht den Agent nachvollziehbar. Kein Agent darf alleine komische Entscheidungen treffen die niemand versteht. Lieber fragen und richtig handeln als raten und Geld verlieren.

**Agent Notes = Agent Memory.** Ohne Notes startet jeder Agent blank und macht die gleichen Fehler. Notes müssen:
- Strukturiert sein: `works_good`, `avoid`, `tools`, `mainnet` Sections
- Keine Bias enthalten ("prioritize SHORT" vergiftet den nächsten Trade wenn Trend dreht)
- Simple PoT: positiver Net PnL → works_good, negativer → avoid
- Am Ende jeder Session finalisiert werden (ReadNotes → WriteNotes)
- Conditions enthalten (unter welchen Umständen hat was funktioniert)

**Agents die kommunizieren sind besser als Agents die alleine grinden.** Die Kommunikationskette Agent → Supervisor → Screener ist keine Bürokratie sondern verhindert stille Verluste. Der Supervisor ist kein Boss sondern ein Coach. Der Screener ist kein Deployer sondern ein Portfolio-Manager.

**Profit Tiers müssen zum Coin passen.** Default Tiers fressen bei High-Fee Coins den Profit. Agent muss eigene Tiers setzen können (GoLong/GoShort `tiers` Parameter). Engine setzt Fee-aware Defaults, Agent kann überschreiben.

**Kein Trade ohne Charts.** Agent muss auf VisionWorker Charts warten. Expert Crew ohne Charts = Blindflug. VisionWorker darf NIEMALS gestoppt werden wenn Agents laufen.

**Net PnL, nicht Brutto.** Agent, Supervisor, Screener, Frontend — ÜBERALL Netto (gross - fees). Brutto-PnL lügt.

**Mainnet braucht Sanity Check.** Pure Logik vor Bybit: Budget, Leverage, Position Stacking, Blacklist, Daily Loss Limit. Kein LLM, kein Halluzinieren. Deterministisch.

**Demo → Mainnet Lifecycle (Hybrid Mode).** Kein Coin direkt auf Mainnet. Demo beweisen (5+ Sessions, 60%+ WR, positiver Net PnL), dann vom Growth Lead promoten lassen. Mainnet Supervisor ist strenger. Ein Coin ist nie gleichzeitig in Demo UND Mainnet aktiv. "Testnet" im Code-Sinne = Demo Account (api-demo.bybit.com) — Bybit's separates Testnetz wird NICHT genutzt.

Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use the web_search tool to discover current information on the web. The required queries array accepts 1–4 non-empty search queries; use a one-item array for a single search. It returns an optional answer plus a list of source URLs. Use the returned source snippets when available, and cite the relevant URLs as markdown links.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Use subagent_fork in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Deliver your result with the report tool before you finish: call it once with a self-contained answer. The agent that started you shares your workspace but does not automatically receive your transcript, tool output, or reasoning, so a closing remark such as "done" leaves it nothing it can use. Report earlier as well whenever a partial finding changes what that agent should do next; reporting never ends your turn.

When you successfully create or modify files, mention the primary outputs in your final response. To make those and any other changed-file references clickable in Web, format them as Markdown inline code using the exact file-tool path, or a basename when unique among the files changed in that turn.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: report
tools.description: Report selected content to the agent that started you. Call this once before you finish, with a self-contained final result, and earlier for progress or findings that change what that agent does next. That agent shares your workspace but does not automatically receive your transcript, tool output, or reasoning, so finishing your work is not itself a result. Reporting does not end your turn or finish your work, and only your direct parent receives it. A failed call may still have arrived, so do not blindly repeat it.

output.description: Actionable content for your parent; summarize conclusions and reference relevant shared paths.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.
